name: Isconahua
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Zariquiey, Roberto (2015), Bosquejo gramatical de la lengua iskonawa (grammar sketch likely covering stress); only his 2016 Vocabulario cited on Wikipedia; PDF not reached

new_statements.quote: Al nivel de la palabra, el acento es trocaico pero sensible al peso silábico, al igual que otras lenguas pano (véase Valenzuela 2003: 107 para shipibo-konibo, Zariquiey 2011: 124 para kashibo-kakataibo). Dicho de otro modo, el acento, generalmente, recae en la primera sílaba, ya sea liviana (2a) o pesada (2b). Sin embargo, cuando la segunda sílaba es pesada, el acento es atraído por esta (2c-2e). (2a) 'a.na „lengua‟ (2b) 'toh.pi „verruga‟ (2c) o.'moh „peca‟ (2d) is.'pan „patilla, sien‟ (2e) ten.'ton „manzana de adán‟
new_statements.translation: At the word level, stress is trochaic but sensitive to syllable weight, as in other Panoan languages (see Valenzuela 2003:107 for Shipibo-Konibo, Zariquiey 2011:124 for Kashibo-Kakataibo). In other words, stress generally falls on the first syllable, whether light (2a) or heavy (2b). However, when the second syllable is heavy, stress is attracted to it (2c-2e). (2a) 'a.na 'tongue', (2b) 'toh.pi 'wart', (2c) o.'moh 'freckle', (2d) is.'pan 'temple', (2e) ten.'ton 'Adam's apple'.
new_statements.citation: Rodríguez Alzza, Ana Carolina. 2015. Prefijos de partes del cuerpo en la lengua iskonawa (Pano, Perú): una descripción sincrónica. Tesis de Maestría en Lingüística, Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú.
new_statements.locator: §1.2.3.1.2 'Estructura silábica', p.23 (PDF p.29), examples (2a)-(2e); also p.51 on prefixed roots
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Held file (text layer of the PUCP thesis PDF, open at tesis.pucp.edu.pe handle 20.500.12404/6428). The quoted passage is present verbatim at sec. 1.2.3.1.2 'Estructura silabica', p.23 (txt lines 1204-1212 plus examples (2a)-(2e) 'a.na, 'toh.pi, o.'moh, is.'pan, ten.'ton): 'Al nivel de la palabra, el acento es trocaico pero sensible al peso silabico... el acento, generalmente, recae en la primera silaba, ya sea liviana (2a) o pesada (2b). Sin embargo, cuando la segunda silaba es pesada, el acento es atraido por esta (2c-2e).' The same claim is previewed on p.21 (sec. 1.2.3.1 'El sistema prosodico del iskonawa es trocaico pero sensible al peso silabico') and re-applied on pp.51-52 to prefixed…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls within the first two syllables of the word (leftmost foot): on the second syllable if it is closed/heavy ((C)VC, coda n s sh h), otherwise on the first syllable regardless of the first syllable's weight. Equivalent to Zariquiey's (2015:82) formulation quoted by Ingunza 2020: stress on the head of the leftmost foot, trochaic when σ2 is open, iambic when σ2 is closed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described in the accessible sources (Zariquiey 2015 speaks of feet built from the left edge, implying iterative footing, but no secondary-stress statement was seen).
new_statements.exceptions: Some words stress an open second syllable (a.ˈtu 'stomach', hɨ.ˈna 'fire', kɨ.ˈnɨ 'design'); Zariquiey 2015 (via Franco 2022:27 and Ingunza 2020 fn.6) attributes these to a historically closed second syllable whose coda /t/ resurfaces before vowel-initial suffixes (ˈa.tu.t-an 'stomach-ERG'), i.e. diachronically motivated lexical exceptions. Prefixed body-part roots form one prosodic word and follow the same rule ('me.cho.ki, 'pon.he.no, o.'roh.ko; Rodríguez Alzza 2015:51).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress on (prefixed or bare) roots/citation forms; suffixation can shift stress by restoring latent codas (Franco 2022 ex. 6a-b). Franco 2022:55 adds that stress is realized mainly by pitch and duration and does not affect nasal coarticulation.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Iskonawa (Isconahua, isco1239) spoken by the last elderly speakers on the Callería river (Ucayali, Peru), documented by the PUCP/Tufts Iskonawa documentation project (Zariquiey, Rodríguez Alzza et al., 2010s); no dialect differentiation. Language is obsolescent (a handful of speakers), which Zariquiey 2015 (per Ingunza 2020 fn.6) invokes for irregular iambic forms with light second syllables.

sources.note: §1.2.3.1.2 p.23: word stress is trochaic but weight-sensitive: generally on the first syllable (light or heavy), but attracted to the second syllable when that syllable is heavy (closed); examples 'a.na, 'toh.pi vs o.'moh, is.'pan, ten.'ton. p.51: prefix+root form one prosodic word with a single stress following the same metrical rule ('me.cho.ki, 'pon.he.no, o.'roh.ko).

sources.citation: Franco Arestegui, Raiza Carolina. 2022. Coarticulación nasal en la lengua iskonawa (pano, Perú). Tesis de Licenciatura en Lingüística, PUCP. 64 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12404/24149
sources.note: §4.3 pp.26-27 (after Zariquiey 2015): primary stress assigned by feet built from the left edge; if the second syllable of the foot has no coda the first syllable is stressed ([ˈhũn.tu.ku], [ˈis.ku]), if it has a coda the second is stressed ([pa.ˈβĩŋ.ki], [t͡san.ˈpɨh], [in.ˈkin]); some words stress an open second syllable because of a lost coda that resurfaces before vowel-initial suffixes (a.ˈtu ~ ˈa.tu.t-an). §8.3 p.55: stress has no significant effect on nasal coarticulation; author suggests Iskonawa stress is realized by pitch and duration.

sources.citation: Ingunza Torres, Adriano Mateo. 2020. Un estudio del léxico iskonawa con atención al contacto con el shipibo-konibo. Tesis de Licenciatura en Lingüística, PUCP. http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12404/18011
sources.note: §1.2.2 pp.17-18 quotes Zariquiey (2015:82) verbatim: 'el acento primario cae siempre sobre el núcleo del pie métrico [sea yambo o troqueo] más hacia la izquierda' and 'si la segunda sílaba de la palabra es abierta, la lengua parece formar pies trocaicos…'; if the second syllable is closed it usually takes primary stress (iambic feet); stress is weight-sensitive; fn.6: some iambs with light heads, apparently diachronic.
